payload.description:
## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-28: operations need an observability surface, not only a live wall. The ledger already records every dispatch (`[harness-run]` markers with tokens, cost, duration, outcome), every gate result, every rework and every scope violation. Nothing renders them over time. The handover of 2026-08-27 computed the bottlenecks by hand: 95 merge-gate reworks, landing failures by check (pytest 44, lint-imports 24, docs-claims 16), 303 scope violations, a 24 percent lane failure rate over 441 runs. An operator should read those numbers off the board, not off a session transcript.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an operator opens `/ops` on the board, IT SHALL show, for a selectable window of 1, 7 and 30 days: lanes dispatched, landed, failed and reworked; tokens and cost per landed record; the failing verify checks ranked by count; scope violations by path prefix; and median lane duration.
- WHEN a number is shown, IT SHALL name the ledger population it was computed over (record count and event kinds), so a reader can re-derive it with the kit CLI.
- WHEN the ledger holds no event in the window, the tile SHALL say `no data` and never render zero as a measurement.
- WHEN the page renders, IT SHALL read the folded ledger and the `[harness-run]` markers only; it SHALL spawn nothing and hold no lock.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_*.py`
- `src/basicly/usage_*.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/board/**`
- `tests/test_board_*.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>`, open `/ops`, and compare the 7-day rework count against `jq -c 'select(.kind=="comment" and (.payload.text|test("harness-policy\\] rework")))' .basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl | wc -l` for the same window.

payload.description:
## Context

Plan §7.3 - a decision owed by the owner, before Phase 6 writes code. Cannot be derived from the code.

beads_rust is MIT with an OpenAI/Anthropic rider restricting a class of users (the licence correction recorded in the closed q5pk review), which is itself the strongest argument for owning the component - architecture §14.5.

A clean-room boundary therefore applies: the replacement must not be derived from beads_rust source. Sanctioned inputs are our own ledger observable data, the documented br CLI contract, and the genuine-MIT upstream original.

Confirm the boundary with someone qualified before implementation proceeds. The conservative line costs nothing because the MIT original is available.

No dependency edge yet - the event-log build beads are deliberately unfiled until vkh0.2 freezes the surface. Wire this as their blocker at the Phase 6 decomposition.
payload.title: Obtain the clean-room boundary sign-off before the tracker replacement writes code

payload.text:
[harness-info] Clean-room boundary signed off by the repo owner, 2026-07-26. This is the owner determination required by docs/plan/implementation-plan.md §7.3, not a legal opinion.

Sanctioned inputs for the tracker replacement:
- our own ledger observable data - the committed .beads/issues.jsonl export, run records, and the behaviour we have measured through the CLI;
- the documented br CLI contract - subcommands, flags, exit codes and output shapes as published, which is what vkh0.1 records and vkh0.2 freezes;
- the genuine-MIT upstream original.

Prohibited: deriving any part of the replacement from beads_rust source. beads_rust is MIT with an OpenAI/Anthropic rider restricting a class of users, which is itself the strongest argument for owning the component (architecture §14.5). The conservative line costs nothing because the MIT original is available.

Phase 6 may now write code within this boundary. The defects recorded in vkh0.6 are requirements input for the replacement, derived from our own observed behaviour rather than from reading source.

payload.description:
## Context
When a person passes a backlog URL such as https://<token>@github.com/owner/repo.git, git_runner.remote_url accepts it, although its refusal text promises no password or token; the URL would then be stored and printed. Found by the round-2 security grader of the M5 design on 2026-11-12 and confirmed by a probe: https, ssh and scp forms with a token user are accepted; user:password is refused. I want https URLs to carry no user part and ssh or scp URLs only a short login name, so a token never enters tracker data. Fixes slice S1 code of M5 (basicly-gtb19bg.43).

`basicly-u2hl.59` added `handoff.PRODUCERS`, which declares every named artifact kind against the
symbol that records it. `HANDOFF_KINDS` in the test suite is now a **second enumeration of the same
set**, and nothing binds the two.

## Context
When a test imports a helper from another test module, I want the kit modules to stay loaded once per worker, so a new test cannot break unrelated tests only in the full xdist suite.

## Finding
On 2026-11-16 tests/test_git_hooks/test_tracker_commit_msg_vault.py imported tests.test_kit_ledger_freeze. Targeted runs passed, but the full suite with -n 4 failed 23 kit tests (quality-gates 43926117616), for example issubclass(InvalidEdgeError, InvalidEventError) False. A full-suite bisect without that file passed them. Fixed by 8dfeb897, which drives the kit through subprocesses.

## Scope note
A blanket refusal of 'from tests.' does not fit: 238 test files import other test modules and pass. The trigger here was a test in the tests/test_git_hooks/ subpackage importing a top-level test module that loads kit modules with spec_from_file_location. The exact mechanism is not proven. The test-discipline skill does not cover it.

## Proposed control
Find the mechanism first, then gate it: for example a conftest check that fails a worker when a kit module name in sys.modules is replaced by a second load. Not claimed and not built.

payload.description:
## Re-scoped 2026-08-04

**The derivation half of this bead moved to basicly-o486.** That bead replaces
`DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX`'s derivation-from-the-largest-completed-estimate with a bound computed
from the resolved runner's trigger and a quantile of the measured `context_tokens` samples, which
removes the self-declared input this bead was filed about. It is itself blocked on basicly-23ep,
because the trigger it divides is currently wrong by a factor of five. Both halves in one lane would
put two diffs on the same constant in `config.py`, so they are separated by file rather than by
intent.

**What survives here is the half the bead never actually carried.** `config.py:455-457` records
it: a pass shares one `.beads` through the redirect, so when basicly-tcmy.5's finishing record
failed the tracker-wide ceiling gate, basicly-tcmy.6 and basicly-tcmy.22 failed verify on
tcmy.5's declaration too and **each was charged a rework attempt for a defect in neither
diff**, against a cap of 2. That is a gate-accounting defect, not a sizing one: a shared
tracker-wide gate must attribute its failure to the lane whose declaration invalidated it, and
must not consume a sibling's bounded rework budget. It is the same shape as basicly-m4zv.14,
where a machine-global lock charged rework for a flake, and it should be resolved consistently
with it.

The original filing follows unchanged, as the evidence for both halves.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX = " src/basicly/config.py
uv run python -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests')
import test_decompose as T
c = T.completed_lane_estimates(T.REPO_ROOT)
print(sorted(c.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:3])"
```

Observed - the largest completed estimate, which is the sole input to the ceiling, is whichever lane declared the widest `## Scope` and finished. Expected - a lane cannot move a global constant by editing its own bead.

## Context

`DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` is derived from the dispatch record: the largest estimate on a completed headless lane, rounded to a floor-unit. The estimate is `seed x scope_read_cost(repo_root, globs)` where the globs come from the lane's **own** `## Scope` section, which the lane itself may rewrite while it runs.

`basicly-fcls` did exactly that. It was dispatched with three globs and an estimate of 94912 under the old measure; it finished having rewritten its scope to nine globs, which under its own new read-capped measure records as 72000 - larger than the 53004 of `basicly-tcmy.31` it had just derived 56000 from. The gate fired against the constant the same lane had committed minutes earlier, which is the gate working correctly.

Two distinct defects sit here, and only the second is about the number.

1. **The derivation is a ratchet with a self-declared input.** It can only ever be dragged upward, and the lever is a field the lane controls. A lane that names ten files it barely touches raises the ceiling for every future lane, with no human deciding and no evidence that a lane that size can actually run. Nothing bounds this.

2. **A lane's scope may change after it is admitted.** The band admits a lane on the scope it declared at dispatch, and the record is written against the scope it declared at finish. Those are different quantities and are compared as if they were one - the defect class of `basicly-z2wi`, `basicly-3w44` and `basicly-ipx2`. `basicly-jr0l.54` already covers verifying the declared scope at landing and is the natural home for the enforcement half.

The honest counter-argument, so it is not lost: widening the scope was *correct behaviour*. The lane genuinely did need `runner.py` to record `context_tokens`, and declaring it is what the scope field is for. The defect is that an honest declaration silently moved a global constant and made the bead undispatchable at 329606 - so the current design punishes accurate scope reporting.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
payload.title: A shared tracker gate charges every sibling lane rework for one lanes declaration

payload.text: First measurement from RunRecord.context_tokens, which landed with basicly-fcls - and it is a 5x gap, not a 1.5x one. basicly-8ry8 declared a scope costing 8000 read-capped tokens, so the band sized it at 16000 at the bug seed of 2.0, and the lane recorded context_tokens=80211. Occupancy is 5.01x the estimate the band gates on. Three session lanes for the record: 8ry8 est 16000 cost 2393339 occupancy 80211; ipx2 scope 29884 cost 3986470; fcls scope 46066 cost 15245717. This is the first (estimate, measured-occupancy) pair the repo has ever held for the quantity the ceiling is denominated in, and it says the ambient term basicly-fcls declined to invent is the dominant one - consistent with its R^2 of 0.095 for scope against occupancy versus 0.863 for turn count. Do not fit a factor to this single pair; it is one sample and the point of the field is to stop declaring what should be measured. Collect pairs first.

Second instance, measured 2026-08-03, and it has a blast radius the first did not.

basicly-tcmy.5 was admitted on eight globs at 66780 working-set tokens. It widened its own ## Scope mid-flight to sixteen, completed the work, and its finishing record then sized 130780 against a ceiling of 72000 - so the separating gate failed and its rework re-dispatch was refused before it started (130780 above the ceiling), which is the trap: a lane that grows past the band cannot be re-dispatched to finish or fix anything.

**The new finding is the cascade.** Every lane in a supervised pass shares one .beads through the redirect, and the ceiling gate asserts over the whole tracker rather than over the lane's own diff. So tcmy.5's scope edit failed verify for basicly-tcmy.6 and basicly-tcmy.22 too, and each was charged rework 1/2 for a defect in neither diff. That is basicly-55yh's principle (an infrastructure failure must not spend a lane's rework budget) reached by a different mechanism: not flakiness, a genuine global gate failing on a sibling's data. Any fix for this bead should say what a pass does when one lane's declaration invalidates a shared gate - hold the pass, or scope the gate to the lane.

Resolved for now at b6c5685 by deriving the ceiling to 132000 from tcmy.5's completion, per the rule the constant's own comment states, with the ratchet recorded rather than hidden. That unblocks the three lanes; it does not fix this bead. The ratchet still has a self-declared input and a lane can still move a global constant by editing its own bead.

One related defect found while reconciling and fixed in the same commit: the gate's population counted a decider dispatch as a completed lane. A decision is recorded against whichever bead raised it, so the escalation on the basicly-tcmy epic sized the epic's whole surface at 1344546 and demanded a ceiling of 1352000 - from a dispatch that wrote no code. Phase-filtered now, with a control that fails when the filter is removed.

payload.text:
[requirements v3, part 1 of 3]

# Meta harness requirements, version 3 (2026-11-04)

## Goal

One terminal-first interface through which the owner never again runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot or another agent CLI directly. It orchestrates, delegates, exchanges messages between and controls those vendor harnesses on the owner's own subscriptions, shares one persistent memory, and survives terminal restarts like herdr. Example: analyze with Codex gpt-6.1-sol, design with Claude Code Opus 5.5, implement with Copilot kimi-k3.

## Verified facts (2026-11-04; rung 2 installed binary, 3 vendor docs, 6 third-party repo)

- Claude Code 2.1.318, unmodified binary: `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose`; `--resume`, `--session-id`, `--fork-session`; `--model`, `--effort`; `--mcp-config` with `--strict-mcp-config`; `--permission-prompt-tool mcp__server__tool` or `stdio` (stdin control_request); interrupt by SIGINT or stdin `interrupt` (idle-tested only); cost and usage in output; `rate_limit_event` documented, not observed. A pending approval does not survive a process restart. Under `--safe-mode` the reported permission mode was `auto`. Rung 2 and 3.
- Anthropic text: no third-party claude.ai login or plan routing "on behalf of their users"; no collecting, storing or intermediating Claude.ai credentials or session tokens; an end user may sign in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription; "Advertised usage limits for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK." Rung 3.
- Codex 0.166.0: `codex app-server` JSON-RPC (experimental): thread/resume, turn/interrupt, approval requests, approvalPolicy, model/list and per-turn model, rate limits and token usage, MCP per thread. Restoring a pending approval after a restart not established. OpenAI terms on third-party automation of a ChatGPT plan not established; auth doc points programmatic use to API keys. Rung 2 and 3.
- Copilot 1.0.105: `copilot --acp --stdio`; initialize reports loadSession true, MCP http and sse, session list and close, auth method copilot-login; cancel is the base `session/cancel` notification (honoured: not established); model change via `session/set_config_option` (not established); `kimi-k3` listed. GitHub terms: no automation clause beyond no "excessive automated bulk activity". Rung 2 and 3.
- herdr 0.9.5 (Apache-2.0): closing the client keeps processes alive; after processes die it restores the layout and resumes agents that reported a session reference. Whether a custom pane can report one programmatically: not established. Rung 3.
- T3 Code (MIT): reference for Codex app-server and Copilot ACP message shapes only; its own ChatGPT OAuth broker conflicts with R0. Rung 6.
- basicly ledger: one append-only shard per writer, merged by git union, plus a process lock; catalog projection to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md exists. Rung 5.

## Decisions taken

D1 Drive only official vendor clients with the owner's own login, on the owner's machine, for the owner's own use.
D2 Transports: Codex app-server; Copilot ACP; Claude Code binary in stream-json print mode. T3 Code is a reference, not a dependency.
D3 Memory is the basicly ledger through the tracker kit, plus catalog projection.
D4 Engines talk through the meta harness as an MCP server; every verified engine supports MCP, so there is no file fallback in v1.

## Requirements for v1

R0 Legal. Each adapter cites the vendor text that permits its path, with the date checked; it does not ship without one. The meta harness never implements a vendor login and never collects, stores, forwards or brokers a vendor credential; first-run setup shows the vendor's own login command. It is for the owner's own use and is not offered to other users.

[requirements v3, part 2 of 3]

R1 Adapters. Contract: start, resume, send turn, stream events, answer approval, interrupt, choose model, report usage. Each declares its approval channel (native, prompt-tool, unsupported), its unsupported operations and its supported vendor version range, checked by a handshake at start and before each workflow. An unknown event or method is an error shown to the owner. A vendor binary outside the declared range is refused by name with the upgrade or pin command.

R2 Isolation. Each engine session runs inside a boundary the harness owns (separate OS user, container or bubblewrap) whose only writable root is its step worktree. It cannot read or write the ledger, the audit log, sibling worktrees, the meta harness state, or another vendor's credentials and binaries. An engine that cannot run this way is disabled by name. Engines are launched with a harness-generated, engine-read-only configuration that forces ask-or-deny, sets the permission mode explicitly, and refuses bypass flags; the adapter re-reads the effective mode before every turn.

R3 Workflow. The owner writes or edits a step list (engine, model, permission profile, inputs, outputs, file scope); a planner may draft it read-only within a stated cap, and engines and models the owner names are binding. A preflight at confirmation checks login, model availability, version range and isolation for every step and reports all failures at once with fix commands. Nothing runs before confirmation. Steps run one at a time in v1. Each step's status (planned, dispatched, completed, failed, interrupted) is written before dispatch; a rerun resumes at the first incomplete step; a workflow with a failed step never reports done.

R4 Context and artifacts. Each step receives the projected rules for its engine, the artifacts named as its inputs and nothing else. Artifacts are files in a per-workflow folder with a declared name and format, recorded in the ledger by the step that produced them.

R5 Memory. Memory writes go through the basicly tracker kit with the step id recorded; the kit's sharding and lock are the concurrency control. write_memory returns a committed record id only after a durable write, else an error. Engine writes are notes that are never projected as rules; a rule or catalog change is a proposal shown as a diff for owner approval. Secret scanning runs on every memory write, log line and stored transcript.

R6 Messaging. MCP tools delegate, ask, read_memory, write_memory, report, reachable only through the engine's own session channel. Inter-engine messages are untrusted data marked with their origin and never enter the receiver's rules. A delegated step runs with the overlap of caller and target permissions. ask has a depth limit, a timeout that returns timed-out, and a visible child session shown under its parent with engine and model.

R7 Approvals. Only the meta harness answers an approval, bound to a nonce, the action and the session; the first answer wins. An approval shows engine, step, delegation chain and diff; the owner may allow an action class for one step. A pending approval blocks only its session, raises a notification, and after a configured timeout is denied and the step marked blocked with a retry command. Approvals never carry over a restart; voided approvals are listed. Each privileged action and its approval is recorded in the ledger.

[requirements v3, part 3 of 3]

R8 Sessions and resumption. Engine processes run under herdr, or a harness supervisor if herdr cannot host them, so closing the interface stops nothing. The service starts with the owner's login session, or is started by the client, which says so (including WSL). After a host restart each session reopens at its last completed turn through the vendor's resume; a turn with unknown outcome is shown as interrupted, with the reason, the kept worktree diff and the choices rerun from last artifact, rerun clean, take over by hand, or abandon. It is never re-sent automatically.

R9 Interface. A chat line, slash commands and keys, with a help screen listing every command. One timeline with each line labelled by engine, model and step. Each session shows one state: running-tool, awaiting-approval, awaiting-reply, awaiting-quota, idle, stalled, interrupted, with the last event time; a missing heartbeat for N seconds turns it stalled with a reason. A since-last-seen summary on start. A review screen per workflow with artifacts, diff, verification result, cost per engine and approvals, offering accept with commit, rework a step, or discard. A take-over command opens the vendor client on the step's own session and reattaches it afterwards. Every error names the next command. The control server listens only on a user-only socket with peer checks; engines have no route to it.

R10 Usage. Each figure is marked vendor-reported, estimated or unknown. At a quota limit the step waits as awaiting-quota with the reset time or unknown and offers wait, switch model, switch engine, or stop; no automatic move in v1.

## Moved to later versions

Parallel steps and merge; automatic engine move and spend caps; web, desktop and phone clients; plugin hot reload; signed adapters and recorded-transcript contract tests; hash-chained or externally anchored audit; vendor-specific screens; remote engines.

## Open owner questions

Q1 Whether heavy automated orchestration of the Claude subscription counts as ordinary, individual usage.
Q2 Isolation mechanism and its cost (separate OS user, container, bubblewrap) on WSL and Windows.
Q3 herdr as process host, pending the custom-pane session reference check.
Q4 OpenAI terms for automating a ChatGPT plan through app-server.

[requirements v4, part 1 of 2]

# Meta harness requirements, version 4 (2026-11-04)

Changes from v3: isolation names bubblewrap and exposes each engine's own home; herdr hosts panes through report-agent-session; daily-use and overhead acceptance added; nightly vendor contract test back in v1; unknown notifications pass through; the nine v3 conflicts resolved; vague terms given values. Open owner questions at the end.

## Goal

One terminal-first interface through which the owner never again runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot or another agent CLI directly. It controls those vendor harnesses on the owner's own subscriptions, delegates and exchanges messages between them, shares one persistent memory, and survives restarts. Success is measured by daily use (R11), not by features.

## Verified facts added in round 3 (2026-11-04, this machine)

- bubblewrap 0.11.2 with unprivileged user namespaces: one writable root, hidden paths, read-only /usr confirmed. Docker 29.1.3 and rootless Podman 5.7.0 usable. A separate OS user needs interactive sudo: refuted.
- Vendor sandboxes confine the commands an engine runs, not the engine's own file tools (Claude, Copilot docs); Codex read restriction not established.
- Credential locations: Claude `~/.claude` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; Codex `~/.codex` or `CODEX_HOME` or keyring; Copilot system store or `~/.copilot`, `COPILOT_HOME`. Login inside bwrap: not tested.
- herdr 0.9.5: `herdr pane report-agent-session ... -- RESUME_ARG` registers a resume command; `pane list`, `agent.list` and `pane.agent_status_changed` report state; client restart keeps processes; herdr server restart does not, it reruns the resume command.
- Run records today: claude 567, manual 294, codex 11, copilot 0 dispatches.

## Requirements for v1

R0 Legal. As v3, plus: no adapter is built before its citation exists.

R1 Adapters. As v3, plus: an unknown notification is logged and passed on; an unknown request that needs a reply is an error. A nightly contract test runs each adapter against the latest vendor release and reports a break before the owner meets it.

R2 Isolation. Each engine process runs in a bubblewrap boundary (rootless Podman as fallback) owned by the harness. Writable: its step worktree, the workflow artifact folder, and a private vendor home for that engine only (its CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME or COPILOT_HOME, seeded from the owner's home). Not visible: the ledger, harness state, audit records, sibling worktrees, other vendors' homes and binaries. The vendor's own command sandbox stays on inside it. Launch config is harness-generated and read-only to the engine, sets the permission mode explicitly, and refuses bypass flags by name; the effective mode is read back from the session init event. Preflight runs one unpaid login-status call per engine inside the boundary and a feature-parity check of the owner's MCP servers, skills and memory, and reports every lost feature.

R3 Workflow. As v3, with: planner cap 100,000 tokens or 15 minutes; "nothing runs" means no model turn before confirmation (preflight may start vendor processes). Steps run one at a time; an ask or delegate child session may run while its parent waits. Status values: planned, dispatched, completed, failed, blocked, interrupted.

R4 Context and artifacts. As v3, plus: user-level vendor files are copied into the private vendor home only when the owner lists them.

R5 Memory. As v3, with: durable means shard written with fsync and committed to git; a secret-scan hit refuses the write and names the field.

R6 Messaging. As v3, with: permission overlap is the intersection of a common profile (read paths, write paths, network on or off, tool allowlist); ask depth 2, timeout 900 s; each MCP call is bound to its session's channel.

[requirements v4, part 2 of 2]

R7 Approvals. As v3, with: action class is a tool name plus a path pattern, such as Edit(src/**); approval timeout 30 minutes; notification by terminal bell and desktop notification where available; privileged action means any write, shell command or network call. During a take-over the owner answers in the vendor client and the harness records the answers afterwards.

R8 Sessions. Each engine runs in a herdr pane that reports its vendor resume command with report-agent-session. Closing the interface keeps processes; after a herdr or host restart each session reopens through its resume command at its last completed turn. The service starts with a systemd user unit, or the client starts it and says so (WSL without systemd). Interrupted turns as v3.

R9 Interface. As v3, with: stalled after 120 s with no event and no CPU time, or 600 s while a tool call is open; the since-last-seen summary lists restart time, each session's state, voided approvals and items waiting on the owner; state list adds blocked.

R10 Usage. As v3, plus: the harness's request rate never exceeds the owner's measured direct-use rate per vendor.

R11 Daily-use acceptance. On a fixed task set the harness median is at most 1.2 times direct wall-clock time and 1.1 times direct tokens. Over 14 consecutive days at least 80 percent of the owner's agent sessions run through the harness, measured from run records.

payload.text:
[merged from basicly-jr0l.28, triage 2026-11-17] Record retro proposals machine-locally without ever injecting them
Acceptance carried over:
## Trigger

When a retro proposal is not yet promoted to the shared catalog, I want it recorded in a git-ignored machine-local inbox that no agent reads, so I can keep a finding from being lost without letting it silently shape a session.

## Context

Plan §7.4, resolved by owner decision 2026-07-26. The decision is made; this bead implements it.

DECIDED: record but never inject. A machine-local file collects retro proposals and is never loaded into any agents context. It is an inbox for a human to review, not guidance.

This is the rung between dropping a retro proposal and asking a human to amend the shared catalog, and the shape was chosen to make the named risk structurally impossible rather than merely bounded. The risk in the plan is bypass by accretion - guidance that shapes a machines sessions while never being reviewed - which is a near neighbour of the recorded non-goal of an agent-writable catalog, where a bad implementation bounces off a gate but a bad fragment is absorbed and silently degrades every later lane. An expiring lane that did shape sessions was considered and rejected on that ground: expiry bounds the exposure without removing it.

So the value kept is that a finding is not lost between sessions. The value deliberately not taken is that it never influences behaviour until a human has promoted it through the normal catalog path and its gates.

## Notes

The file must be git-ignored, and it must not live anywhere a projection or a hook would pick it up as guidance - the whole guarantee is that no agent reads it. Assert that rather than assuming it: a test that the path is absent from every projected output and from every always-on file is what makes the claim checkable.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/`
- `.gitignore`
Why merged: No retro inbox exists (rg 'inbox' in src and session-finish: no hit); self-improvement-retro fragment is status: deprecated. Same 'recorded but never projected' mechanism as qpr2xmr.3.1.

payload.description:
## Context
The rules that govern an orchestrator session and the sessions it directs must travel with the repository, not live in one machine's notes. They become catalog fragments, the orchestrator agent source and an orchestration skill, each with its enforcement: orch commands, hooks and doctor checks. The ruleset is off by default; a committed [orchestration] table in basicly.toml enables it and names the orchestrator member. Workers get the worker-side fragments; only the orchestrator agent gets the orchestrator side. One fragment lists the three classes: ask-first items the orchestrator decides, owner items the person may approve through the orchestrator, and items that stay in the worker's own window. The CI time check is basicly-jxzin95 and is not built here.

payload.text: Requirements from the workspace mail lock incident of 2026-11-18: a lock held by a background wait loop plus a merge with no unlock outlived the landing, and handily's lane waited from 22:16 UTC. The kit lock must have 4 properties. 1. It records the holder pid and an expiry (default TTL 60 minutes, settable). 2. Its listing shows the age and marks a lock stale when the pid is dead or the TTL passed. 3. lock takes over a stale lock and logs the takeover. 4. A with-lock form runs a command and releases the lock on exit, on success and on failure. The workspace fix is filed under dev-196z3 or a new dev record.

## Context

Both v0.10.0 release refusals on 2026-08-28 reached the operator as the last lines of the hook output: once `FAILED: release-notes (0.32s) · checks failed: 32/33` (usable), once `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations · Contracts: 3 kept, 0 broken.` (the tails of two passing checks, pyright and lint-imports). The second carried no check name and no reason, and finding the cause needed a scratch clone. basicly-85cadb recorded the same shape on the supervisor's tracker-sync commit; this record is the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a release commit is refused by a hook, the refusal message SHALL carry every `FAILED:` line and every `checks failed:` summary line from the hook output, and when the hook emitted neither, IT SHALL say so and name the hook id the framework reported as Failed together with the files the framework reports as modified by that hook.
- WHEN the hook output is longer than the message budget, the message SHALL keep the failure lines and drop passing-check lines, never the reverse.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release.py`
- `src/basicly/checkout.py`
- `tests/test_release.py`
- `tests/test_checkout.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: a fixture hook that modifies a file and exits 0 produces a refusal naming the hook and the file.

When the commit-msg hook refuses a subject, I want the error to name the part and the character that broke the rule, so I can fix the subject on the first retry instead of guessing.

The hook prints only 'Commit message does not follow conventional commit format.' Its description rule allows only lowercase letters, digits, spaces and hyphens. In basicly-tgenbu5 an agent twice guessed subject length while the real cause was a dot (v0.29.0) and an underscore (node_modules).

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-A survey 2026-08-14, with the arithmetic closed.

`policy.py` carries at least four nameable responsibilities: gate and checkpoint policy, bead body scaffolding, autonomy grants and spend metering, human wait telemetry, and the confirm-code store.

It has 10 tokens of size headroom and 0.0 percentage points of prose headroom.

## Only one cut clears both gates

```text
slice                lines        tokens   prose    remainder
wait telemetry       2279-2609    3,405    45.7%    fails density
grants and spend     1455-2140    8,126    56.3%    fails density
confirm code         1204-1274      688    32.4%    fails density
body scaffolding      229-330     1,283    67.5%    passes, remainder 57.1%
```

A cut leaves the remainder green only above 57.6% prose. A new module passes only below 50%. The two windows do not overlap, so the move must land in an existing under-cap module.

## The measured home

`dispatch_brief.py` is 2,523 tokens at 37.4% prose. After the merge it is about 3,806 tokens at about 47.6%, under both caps. It is one tier above `policy`, so all four external callers stay legal: `cli.py:2174`, `supervise.py:1056`, `decompose.py:713` and `decompose.py:1888`. Its theme is prose the engine authors.

`scaffolds.py` is not the home. Its charter at `scaffolds.py:1-13` is installer file templates and it declines this content.

## Take the rename while the seam is open

`compose_body` means two things: bead bodies in `policy` and agent markdown at `agents.py:400`. Rename the bead-body one during the move.

## The honest boundary

The wait telemetry is the conceptually cleaner second cut and is not dispatchable today. Its 45.7% prose share fails the density ratchet from either direction. A further split of `policy.py` needs either prose reduction in the remainder or a deliberate frozen-share decision. Neither is in this scope.

## Acceptance

- When the scaffolding functions move, then both size gates pass with no new frozen entry and no raised baseline, and the `policy.py` entry shrinks in the same diff.
- When the four external call sites are compiled, then they resolve against the new home.
- When a bead body is scaffolded for a bug, then the printed body is byte-identical to today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`

## Depends on

The loop-core dead-symbol slice. Its deletions are the only size headroom available for the import line this leaves behind.

## Demonstration

Compare a scaffolded bug body before and after, run both ratchet scripts, and `uv run pytest -q`.

payload.description:
## Context

Found while landing basicly-lelg (2026-07-31) and deliberately left out of scope there, because it is
not among that bead's seven enumerated defects. Same class of error, same file, and it will mislead the
same way.

`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §14 (around line 1320-1325) makes two claims that are now wrong:

1. **"the path-scoped tier is already built ... and no fragment declares one"** — stale. Two fragments
   declare a scope today (`external-review` on `docs/research/**` + `docs/design/**`, and the
   platform-hermetic tests fragment on `tests/**`). The equivalent line at
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125` was already corrected; this one was missed.
2. **"it improves both cost _and_ adherence"** — contradicts the finding basicly-lelg just recorded.
   Scoping is only a cost *reduction* for Claude and Copilot. For codex it is a strict cost
   *increase*: scoped fragments are inlined into `AGENTS.md` at ~1500 chars each (measured 1462 and
   1614), because codex has no glob scoping and nested `AGENTS.md` below the cwd is never loaded. So the
   claim is true for two of three families and false for the third — which is exactly the asymmetry
   `implementation-plan.md:403-409` is careful about and this sentence flattens.

The adherence half of the claim also deserves a look rather than a copy: basicly-agzx.1 measured recall
at 98% / 93%, and Phase 4's own exit criterion was weakened to "recall **not degraded**" precisely
because there is no headroom left to improve. A sentence asserting scoping "improves adherence" sits
badly next to that.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md` around lines 1320-1325.
2. Compare against `.basicly/core/fragments/` (two fragments carry `scope`), against
   `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:125`, and against §7 detail 4 as corrected by basicly-lelg.
3. Observed: the architecture reference says no fragment declares a scope, and that scoping improves
   cost and adherence for everyone. Expected: it names the two fragments that do declare scopes, and
   states the asymmetry — cost falls for claude and copilot, rises for codex — instead of a blanket
   improvement claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture reference section on the path-scoped tier when it is read then it no longer claims that no fragment declares a scope, and the cost claim names the asymmetry between claude and copilot on one side and codex on the other rather than asserting a blanket improvement, with the adherence claim either evidenced against the agzx.1 measurement or dropped

Measured in the source. `board_serve.py:264-270` builds the self-age note (`SELF_AGE`) and two fault notes, joins them into a `banner` of `

` elements and appends the banner to the rendered page, outside the `.wall` grid. The page body is `height: 100vh; overflow: hidden` (template lines 46-50) and the grid's eight rows fill it, so anything appended after the grid lands below the fold on every viewport of 1280 px or more, where the page does not scroll. The two fault notes (`STALE_TEMPLATE_FAULT`, `DROPPED_ROWS_FAULT`) share the fate, and those two are the ones an operator must see: they say the page is lying. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. `uv run basicly board serve --port 8377`, open the page at 1712x1345. 2. Scroll: nothing moves. The last visible row is `EVENTS — ...`. 3. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8377/ | grep -n 'producer age'` prints the line. It exists in the document and never in the viewport. ## Acceptance Criteria - WHEN the server appends its own notes, THEY SHALL render inside the grid's `tick` or `inv` row, so they are visible at every width the layout claims. - WHEN a fault note (`STALE_TEMPLATE_FAULT`, `DROPPED_ROWS_FAULT`) is present, IT SHALL render with the `stale` or `fail` state colour and above the `events` line, never below it. - WHEN no fault is present, the self-age line SHALL render as one dim line and SHALL NOT take a row from `next up`. - WHEN `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` runs against the live document at 1440, 1600 and 1920, IT SHALL report every note inside the viewport. ## Scope - `src/basicly/board_serve.py` - `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2` - `tests/test_board_serve.py` - `tests/test_board_render.py`

payload.description:
## Trigger
Verifying the owner premise that the post-release work is docs only and reaches nobody. It is not: six catalog files reach a consumer, and one of them is inside a wheel.

## The defect
`.basicly/core/kit/tier/README.md` is force-included into the tier wheel at `basicly_tier/kit/README.md`. Its broken link was fixed after v0.13.0 while `packages/basicly-tier` stayed at 0.2.1. `uvx` caches by name and version, so a consumer holding 0.2.1 would never receive the corrected file. The fix was undeliverable.

Bumped to 0.2.2 and proved by rebuilding: the wheel carries the corrected text.

## Third occurrence today
The same class was caught by hand twice before. Once when the model map changed and the tier kit needed 0.2.0. Once when `kit_installer.py` dropped the third skill root and all three kits needed 0.2.1. Each time the check was a person remembering to run it.

## Proposal, not applied
A gate that fails when any path force-included into a package changed since the commit that last moved that package version. The inputs are already declared: each `pyproject.toml` names its `force-include` sources, and git knows when the version line last moved. The check is the one I ran by hand three times.

## Why it matters more than a readme
Nothing about this is specific to documentation. The same silence would cover a fix to `kit_installer.py` or to a resolver, where a consumer keeping the cached wheel keeps the bug.

## Scope
- `packages/basicly-tier/pyproject.toml`
- a new check under `.scripts/`

payload.description:
## Context

R6 in `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md:73` requires that "no committed artifact carries a
host path, username or hostname". It exists because the `br` export wrote
`source_repo_path` on 328 of 332 records.

`.basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` is committed (confirmed with `git ls-files`) and **every
one of its 3,775 events carries `"actor": "<redacted:machine-username>"`**, with `"created_by": "<redacted:machine-username>"` inside
payloads. Absolute paths *are* correctly redacted - 3 hits, all of the form `<redacted:posix-absolute-path><user>/...`
- so the redaction pass works on paths and does not look at the actor field.

No gate sees this: `.basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py` scans for paths (`:42` scopes to
`^\.beads/.*\.jsonl$`) and not for usernames, and its scope does not include
`.basicly/ledger/`. No bead was found covering it.

So the artifact built to satisfy the nine paid-for requirements reproduces one of them, in the
one field the redactor does not read. This is the same class of defect as the `br` export
R6 was derived from.

## Open question this bead must settle first

Whether R6's requirement column is intended to bind the owned ledger's `actor` field at all,
or only host paths. If actor attribution is wanted, it needs a stable non-identifying form
(an opaque per-repo id, or the git author already in the commit) rather than the OS username.

## Proposed check

Extend the path scan to the owned ledger and to usernames, with a positive control: a test
plants a known username in a ledger event and asserts the gate fails, and asserts it passes on
a redacted equivalent.
payload.title: Stop the owned ledger committing a username in every event

payload.text:
[harness-info] closed under owner decision 3a — stop writing it **and** scrub history.

The open question this bead said it had to settle first is answered by that decision:
R6 binds the `actor` field, and the non-identifying form is no form at all. Nothing in
the live path was writing a person there — `br.import_export` defaults `actor` to `""`
and the CLI passes none — so the 3,775 values were the 2026-08-07 hand-run import's.

**The leak was wider than filed, and the wider half is the one still being written.**
The bead measured the ledger. The committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` carried the username
on **813 of 876 records**, because br writes `created_by` on every record it mints and
`migrate._plan_record` copies every non-structural field into the `created` payload
verbatim. So a fresh `basicly tracker import` re-published it. Inside the ledger it sat
on `asserted_by` (3,176), `created_by` (736), `assignee` (56) and 4 free-text values —
not only on `actor`, which is where the bead looked.

**Stop writing it.** `redact.redact_committed` = paths, then identity, and the four
ledger/export write sites in `br.py` use it. The order is load-bearing: the placeholder
holds characters the path rules' tail class excludes, so identity first would leave the
directory layout published. Identity is deliberately outside `MACHINE_PATH_RULES` — a
username is not a shape, only the running machine knows the string — so the mirror test
that holds the hook's rule tuple equal to the module's is untouched.

**Scrub history.** `br.scrub_ledger` rewrote **4,812 of 5,079** events, and
`scrub_export` **811 of 876** records. This is the one place the design edits a line
rather than appending one (work-tracker §4.4); an append cannot un-publish a string,
which is why §4.2 reserves it for an explicit owner decision.

The re-minting is the part that could have gone wrong quietly. An event id covers kind
plus payload, so a redacted payload has to be re-minted or `fsck` reads every scrubbed
event as inconsistent — and the generation the id folds in is **not written on the
line**. It is derived as the occurrence count of an identical (record, kind, payload),
and the derivation was proved before it was used: it reproduced **all 5,079** stored ids
exactly. After the rewrite, all 5,079 re-mint from their own content and there are 0
duplicate ids. `basicly tracker shadow` reports 372 disagreements, **every one
`query='gates'` and excused as history** — the gate-import gap decision 1a covers — and
zero on records, phase or ready.

**The gate.** `tracker-path-scan` now covers `.basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl` beside
`.beads/*.jsonl`, and reports a `machine-username` rule built per run from
`getpass.getuser()`. Positive control, run against the pre-scrub ledger kept for it: the
gate reports **4,812 findings**, which is exactly the count the scrub repaired, and 0 on
the repaired file. Its stated limit: it cannot see a *teammate's* username already in
the file — that is `[[privacy.denied]]`'s job, and this repo configures none.

**What is deliberately left.** 75 occurrences of the git handle `niksavis` survive in
each file. The rule is word-bounded, so a name the username merely prefixes is not
touched — and that handle is this project's own published identity, in the
`git+https://github.com/...` install URL architecture §9 ships. A gate that redacted it
would fight the README.

Verified: 4106 passed; `[verify] PASS (mode: fast)`, 21 checks.
Demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_path_scan_identity.py tests/test_br_scrub_ledger.py -q`
(13 tests). `scrub_ledger` is wired at `merge.commit_tracker_state`, beside `scrub_export`
and on the same commit path, so `wired-or-deleted` and vulture both bind it.

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-D survey 2026-08-14, with the ratchet arithmetic measured at the cut.

`decompose.py:1` declares one responsibility: turn a feature into child issues and a dependency graph. The module cannot be named without the word and. It validates plans, prices working sets, forecasts whole-lane spend and audits forecast accuracy.

It is 24,484 tokens against a frozen 24,498. Fourteen tokens of headroom. The next comment added here trips the gate.

## Measured with the gates' own instruments

```text
whole module                     24,484 tokens   59.1% prose (frozen 59.9%)
spend forecast, lines 1124-1441   3,761 tokens   65.5% prose
```

The cut is prose-heavier than its origin and under the 4,000-token cap, so both ratchets pass by measurement rather than by hope. The remainder lands near 16,900 tokens at about 57.5%.

## What moves

`SpendForecast`, `spend_from_working_set`, `forecast_spend`, `calibration_status`, `spend_forecasts`, `dispatch_spend_forecasts`, `unsized_lane_tokens` and the quantile helper.

Consumers to re-point: `supervise.py:1300`, `supervise.py:1322`, `supervise.py:2602`, `cli.py:2717`, `cli.py:2901`, `usage_report.py:49`.

The new module imports only the run record, the spend calibration and the configuration. Nothing imports back into `decompose`.

## Acceptance

- When the extraction lands, then the named symbols live in one module of at most 4,000 tokens whose prose share does not exceed its measured value at cut time.
- When both size gates run, then `decompose.py` falls below its frozen baseline.
- When any existing consumer calls these functions, then the behaviour is unchanged. This item makes no logic edit.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- a new module
- `src/basicly/supervise.py` imports only
- `src/basicly/cli.py` imports only
- `tests/test_decompose.py`

## Depends on

The corpus correction to the unsized lane bound. That bead rewrites a function this one moves.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`, both ratchet scripts, and `uv run basicly usage forecast`.

- When two clones fold the same ledger input with different machine usernames, the trunk they produce shall be byte-identical, and a test shall pin it.
- When a fold or any tracker commit runs, it shall not rewrite an existing trunk event or change its id; redaction of old events shall happen only through an explicit, host-independent command.
- When a clone pulls and has no local work to push, the post-merge hook shall create no commit.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When any clone folds pending shards after a pull, I want the fold to move the shards into the trunk unchanged, so I can pull on every machine without a local commit that rewrites history.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a consumer repository (terminal, basicly v0.20.2 via uvx), git pull on a second machine. The generated post-merge block basicly-tracker compact runs basicly tracker fold.
2. The fold commits chore(tracker): fold pending writer shards into the trunk log, and main is ahead of origin by 1 on every pull.
3. Besides moving pending-main.jsonl into events-0001.jsonl, the commit rewrites 8 existing trunk events: the local machine username in payload fields such as created_by and in prose becomes the machine-username redaction marker, and each event gets a new id (record term-f0z: origin id ev-c78faed0f8, local fold ev-4903f67ebd). The fold diff is +536/-536 lines.

Cause (read in code): basicly tracker fold commits through merge.commit_tracker_state, which calls tracker.scrub_ledger (src/basicly/merge.py:360). scrub_ledger rewrites every ledger file with the redaction of the host that runs it and re-mints the ids of changed events. The same scrub refuses with does-not-re-mint when an event sits in two shards (seen 2026-10-08 in basicly, basicly-jho04rg).

Reported 2026-10-08 by the owner from the terminal repository; reproduced twice there.
payload.requirements:
- The ledger stays append-only: an event id never changes once committed.
- Keep write-time redaction of new events.
- Standard library only.

payload.description:
## Context

`.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` treats `.basicly/core/schemas/**/*` as a field-consumer site
(`FIELD_SITE_GLOBS`, line 123) and indexes it with `_tokens()` (line 300), which returns **every
identifier-shaped word in the file**. A JSON schema is mostly `description` prose, so ordinary
English counts as a reference to a dataclass field of the same name.

Reproduced 2026-08-13 on `basicly-r4jm`: adding five schema files whose descriptions contained the
English word **holds** made `record-field:basicly.worktree.RemovalVerdict.holds` stop reproducing,
and the gate reported it as a stale baseline entry. `worktree.py` was byte-identical to main.

**The advice is the dangerous part.** The gate says "remove the entry from BASELINE". Obeying it
would delete a real dead-code finding because unrelated prose used a common word - and the entry
could never come back, because the prose stays. That is the same failure shape this script already
documents at lines 90-98 for parallel worktrees: "the gate advice on a stale entry is remove the
entry, so a maintainer following it would empty the baseline and blind the surface permanently".

Exposed field names are any that are also English: `holds`, `result`, `steps`, `level`, `reason`,
`gates`, `claims`, `output`, `delta`. Nine of the 45 baseline entries are words of this shape.

The intent of scanning schemas is sound - a schema **key** named for a field is a real reference.
The defect is scanning the whole file rather than its keys.

## Steps to Reproduce

- On a clean tree, `uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` - passes, 45 known findings.
- Add any file under `.basicly/core/schemas/` containing the word `holds` in a description string.
- Re-run - `record-field:basicly.worktree.RemovalVerdict.holds ... no longer reproduces`.
- Observed: prose marks a field as wired. Expected: only a schema key or enum value does.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py

payload.description:
## Context

Two of seven handoff artifact kinds exist: `implementation-plan` and `change-summary`. The other
five are unbuilt, and their absence is why four of the seven loop roles cannot be invoked - a role
with no schema has nothing a state can validate, so no state dispatches it.

Verified 2026-08-13 with a positive control: `rg change-summary src/ tests/` returns hits, while
`change-shape`, `verification-evidence`, `validation-transcript`, `release-record` and a quoted
`classification` all return zero. The absence is real, not a bad probe.

`artifact_record.py` needs no change - its docstring already states that a seventh artifact adds a
kind rather than a marker name. Schema resolution is by filename, so no registry edit either: the
file must simply be named `<kind>.schema.json`.

`release-record` additionally has no row in the section 8 artifact table, which is a documentation
gap this bead closes alongside the schema.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `rg -l "validation-transcript" src/ tests/` - zero hits, while the same probe for
  `change-summary` hits `handoff.py`, `loop.py` and two test modules.
- Read `factory-loop.md` section 8: seven artifacts are specified and five have no schema file.
- Consequence: `validator`, `curator`, `retrospector` and `reviewer` are authored and unreachable.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/schemas/classification.schema.json`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/change-shape.schema.json`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/verification-evidence.schema.json`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/validation-transcript.schema.json`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/release-record.schema.json`
- `tests/test_handoff_schemas.py`
- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md
